Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 62, verses 1–4:

(p-299) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surat al-Jumu'a

It is Medinan. al-Naqqash mentioned an opinion that it is Meccan, and that is an error on the part of whoever said it, because the matter of the Jews was only in Medina, and likewise the matter of the Friday prayer (al-Jumu'a) never occurred in Mecca at all, I mean its establishment and its prayer. As for the matter of the dispersal (al-infidad), there is no doubt that it was in Medina. al-Naqqash also reported from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that he embraced Islam only in the days of Khaybar.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah, the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered a messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and the Wisdom, though before that they were certainly in clear error.﴾ ﴿And [He raised him] to others of them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ ﴿That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of great bounty.﴾

The discussion of words like those of the first verse has already passed in full. The recitation differed regarding the grammatical case of the attributes at its end. The majority of people read "al-Maliki" in the genitive as an adjective of Allah, and likewise what follows it, (p-300) while Abu Wa'il Shaqiq, Muslima and Abu al-Dinar read "al-Maliku" in the nominative by way of cutting off (al-qat'), and likewise what follows it. Abu al-Dinar also vocalized the qaf of "al-Quddus" with a fatha.

"Al-ummiyyun" is meant to refer to the Arabs. The unlettered (al-ummi) in the language is one who neither writes nor reads, and it is derived from "Umm al-Qura," which is Mecca. This view is weak, because the description "unlettered" according to this would be restricted to the Quraysh. What is meant is rather all the Arabs, and concerning them the Prophet ﷺ said: "Verily we are an unlettered nation; we do not calculate and we do not write; the month is thus and thus," and this verse is an enumeration of the blessing of Allah the Exalted upon them in what He bestowed upon them. "The verses being recited" are the Qur'an. "Yuzakkihim" means: He purifies them from polytheism, and He hopes for good in them. "The Book" is the revealed text being recited, and "the Wisdom" is the Sunna which is upon his tongue, peace and blessings be upon him.

Then Allah the Exalted made manifest the emphasis on the blessing by mentioning their state which had been the opposite of guidance, and that is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿though before that they were certainly in clear error﴾. "Akharin" (others) is in the genitive position as a conjunction with "al-ummiyyin," and in the accusative position as a conjunction with the preceding pronouns. The people differed regarding the two meanings of the Exalted's saying "wa-akharina." Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, and others said: he meant Persia. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: "Who are the others?" So he took the hand of Salman al-Farisi, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "If faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would reach it." Related by Muslim. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: he meant the Romans and the non-Arabs. The saying of the Exalted "from among them" on these two opinions means only humanity and faith, as if He said: and among other people. Mujahid also said, as did 'Ikrima and Muqatil: he meant the Followers from the sons of the Arabs, so the saying of the Exalted "from among them" means lineage and faith. Ibn Zayd, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Ibn Hibban said: by the saying of the Exalted "wa-akharin" he meant all groups of people, and "from among them" is in humanity and faith as we have said, because we find that his sending, peace and blessings be upon him, was to all creation. Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said to the people of Yemen: "You are they."

The saying of the Exalted ﴿lamma yalhaqu﴾ is a negation of what is near to the present state, and the meaning is that they are about to join them. "Lam" had "ma" added to it for emphasis. Sibawayh said: "lamma" is the negation of your saying "qad fa'ala" (he has done), and "lam" is the negation of your saying "fa'ala" (he did) without "qad."

The saying of the Exalted ﴿That is the bounty of Allah﴾ and the verse... is a clarification of the position of the blessing and of His specifying them with it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 62, verses 5–8:

The Exalted's saying:

﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah, but then did not carry it, is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books. Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ ﴿Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are friends of Allah to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Say: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾

"Those who were entrusted with the Torah" are the Children of Israel and the rabbis contemporary with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "Were entrusted" (ḥummilū) means they were charged with carrying out its commands and prohibitions. This is the perfect sense of a person "carrying" a trust (amānah), and it is not carrying on the back, although it is derived from that meaning. He, exalted is He, mentioned that they did not carry it, that is, they did not obey its command and did not stop at its limits, when they denied Muhammad (ﷺ), while the Torah speaks of his prophethood. So every good that did not benefit them from carrying it is like the likeness of a donkey upon which are books. For it, the books and the dung and other things are in one status.

Yaḥyā ibn Ya'mur read ḥamalū with a fatḥah on the ḥā' and the mīm, lightened. Al-Ma'mūn al-'Abbāsī read yuḥammilu with a ḍammah on the yā', a fatḥah on the ḥā', and a shaddah on the mīm, which is open. In the codex of Ibn Mas'ūd (may Allah be pleased with him) it reads kamathali ḥimārin without the definite article. Al-sifr is a book whose pages are gathered and arranged in order. Then He, exalted is He, explained the condition of their likeness and its corruption by His saying: ﴿Wretched is the likeness of the people﴾. The implied construction is: wretched is the likeness, the likeness of the people.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim..."﴾ up to the end of the verse. It is narrated that it was revealed because the Jews of Medina, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appeared, addressed the Jews of Khaybar about his affair, mentioning his prophethood to them. They said to them: "If you see his followers, we will follow you, and if you see his opposition, we will oppose him along with you." Then the reply of the people of Khaybar came, saying: "We are the sons of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and the sons of 'Uzayr, the son of Allah, and among us are the prophets. And when has prophethood been among the Arabs? We are more worthy of prophethood than Muhammad, peace be upon him, and there is no way to follow him." Then the verse was revealed with the meaning: if you are of such a rank with Allah, then wish for it. The departure from this lowly life is more beloved to you, so wish for death, if you are truthful, believing this rank for yourselves.

Then He, exalted is He, informed about them that they will not wish for it, and will not encounter it except with aversion, because of their knowledge of their evil condition before Allah and their distance from Him. This is what is necessary from the wording of the verse. Many of the exegetes (mufassirūn) (exegesis here being tafsir) narrated that Allah, exalted is He, made this verse a miracle for Muhammad (ﷺ), and a dazzling sign. He informed him that if any one of them wished for death within a number of days, he would die and depart from the world. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Wish for death" in the sense of challenge and manifesting the sign. None of them wished for it out of fear of death and confidence in the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Then He, exalted is He, threatened them with the death from which there is no escape for them, and then with what follows it of being returned to Allah, exalted is He. Ibn Mas'ūd (may Allah be pleased with him) read: "tafirrūna minhu mulāqīkum" with the omission of "fa-innahu."

His saying, exalted is He: "fa-yunabbi'ukum," that is, an informing of one who will punish and requite for it with torment. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read: "fatammannaw al-mawt" with a kasrah on the wāw, and likewise Yaḥyā ibn Ya'mur.

Ibn al-Zubayr and al-A'mash read "al-Jum'ah" with a sukun on the mim, and this is a dialect form.

The people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) said: striving is obligatory on the people of the whole city, whoever hears the call and whoever does not, even if its districts are more than three miles away. Abu Hanifa said: it is not obligatory on one whose dwelling is outside the city, such as Zurara from Kufa, since between them there is only the course of a river. And it is not permissible for them to hold it, because among its conditions are a congregational mosque, a dominant ruler, and an established market. Some scholars said: striving is from five miles. Al-Zuhri said: from six miles, and he also said: from four miles, and Ibn al-Munkadir said the same. Ibn 'Umar, Ibn al-Musayyab, and Ibn Hanbal said: striving is obligatory only on the one who hears the call. In this there is room for consideration.

It has the meaning of His saying: ﴿And that man will have only what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39]. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Malik, and others said: "The prayer is only to be attended with tranquillity (al-sakina)." So the striving is by intention, will, and action. And "the remembrance" (al-dhikr) is the admonition of the khutbah. This was said by Ibn al-Musayyab. What supports this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "The angels are at the doors of the mosque on the day of Friday, recording the first and then the first. Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I am one of them."

Abu Muhammad, the judge, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Their names have not come to me in any register that I recall, except that I heard my father, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, say: they are the ten who were given the good news of Paradise. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they see a trade or amusement﴾. The verse was revealed because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing on the minbar delivering the khutbah on Friday, when a caravan (ʿīr) came from Syria carrying food grain (mīra), and its leader was Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi. Mujahid said: it was their custom that a caravan would enter Medina with drums, musical instruments, and shouting behind it. So the caravan entered with the same, and the people of the mosque dispersed to see and hear it, and they left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing on the minbar. Only twelve men remained with him. Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I am one of them."

Abu Muhammad, the judge, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Their names have not come to me in any register that I recall, except that I heard my father, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, say: they are the ten who were given the good news of Paradise. The eleventh is disputed: it was said 'Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, and it was said 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said in the book of al-Tha'labi: eight men remained with him. And it is reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Were it not for these, stones would have been sent down from heaven upon those who dispersed." In another hadith: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you had followed one another until none of you remained, the valley would have flowed with fire upon you." Qatada said: "It has reached us that they did this three times, because the arrival of the caravan coincided with Friday, since the stages of the journey would bring it about."

His saying, exalted is He: "ilaiha" (to it), and He did not say "ilaihima" (to them both), giving priority to what is more important, since it was the caravan that was the cause of the amusement, and the amusement was not the cause of the caravan. In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, it reads: "wa-min al-tijara lilladhina ittaqaw wallahu khairu al-raziqin" (and from the trade, for those who fear Allah; and Allah is the best of providers).

Consider: if trade is placed before "seeing," that is because it is more important, and it is delayed with the comparative "better" so that the soul first falls upon what is clearer.

In this verse is the standing of the khatib. The first to rest during the khutbah was 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, and the first to deliver the khutbah sitting was Mu'awiya, may Allah be pleased with him. "Al-Raziq" (the Provider) is an attribute of action, and some human beings may be described by it figuratively when they are the means of an animal's provision, while Allah, the Exalted, is the best of providers.

The tafsir of Surat al-Jumu'ah is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
